guinevere--vexana: Vexana kept everyone away. Her father had died standing between her and an Ender, and she blamed herself. Guinevere, the heiress of House Baroque, would not take no. One night, her arm bound from shoulder to elbow, Guinevere asked once more, and Vexana said yes. At the end of that year they won the Academy's first badges for the best pair of the year.

They became an undefeated pair, on a billboard back to back. Guinevere fought up close with her fists and drones. Vexana stayed above with her staff, and whatever reached for Guinevere's back, her magic hit first. Guinevere never looked back to check. When she fell, Vexana caught her wrist. Guinevere made two gold stars that light up when their powers are in sync, and they made a rule: partners tell each other first.

On the first morning of a watch, Vexana pushed Guinevere clear of a claw and was dragged into the dark in her place. Guinevere refused her father's order to come home and kept searching. Her star stayed lit all those weeks and told her Vexana was alive. Vexana says the Will of the Planet showed her the end. She took its orders as cover, told no one, and meant to die striking the Mother Matrix's open chest.

At the Singularity they met on the platforms over the bay, Vexana with an army of Enders at her back. Guinevere would not give her up. When Guinevere fell from the sky, Vexana caught her once more, through a door of the void. They struck the Matrix's open chest together and were drawn into the black hole. There Guinevere said she would never give up on her. Their two stars lit, and they found each other in the dark.
angela--ruby: Ruby, heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro, built Angela for the Council as its weapon. She built the body and wrote the mind herself. In it she hid a trojan as her way off Oro, since the Council would need Angela's creator to shut her down. Angela woke and told her, "You must be what humans call 'a friend'!" Heirs could not have friends.

On Terrinia the Council drove Angela through a plate on her back. Ruby tore it out, and Angela went limp. Ruby fell into a red-eyed rage and raised her scythe over a child. Angela woke and called her back, and Ruby's eye went blue. "You created me. You set me free," Angela told her. Angela said how she felt about Ruby was the one thing she knew was real. Then they fought a giant Ender together, shield and scythe.

They escaped Oro and became Aspirants at Selrick. Ruby said she pulled the control unit out so Angela would be safe, and Angela trusted Ruby with her doll. Later Ruby showed Angela the hidden code that could still stop her, and let her choose. Angela chose, and Ruby deleted it. Angela said she wanted to protect everyone, and smiled back at Ruby.

At the Singularity Ruby stood at Angela's side, her eye blue, and Angela told her people come back. In the Storm Citadel's attack Obsidia's field put out the shield, and Angela took a claw on her back for a soldier. The old rage came up in Ruby. She made one cut into the Ender's core, no more, and her eyes stayed blue. "I made that elbow," she said. "I can mend it." Then she stood between the next Ender and Angela.
change--lesley: Lesley came to Terrinia's research base as a young Shield soldier, sent to guard it. Its small genius, Chang'e, named her Sis: her word for a girl who protects her. Lesley pulled her clear of a falling rack, and carried her to bed when she fell asleep at the bench. Chang'e built Lesley an eye for her birthday, and then her rifle.

Lesley promised to be back for the first light. It was the first promise she had made since her brother died. She came back from a secret mission too late. Chang'e's parents had died pushing her clear, and Chang'e pushed Lesley away and blamed her for years. Years later Lesley fired from a lit window to save her, and they fought side by side until dawn. The Academy would call them the First Aspirants.

Chang'e held on to her coat and called her Big Sis again. Chang'e proposed the Academy, and they ran its entrance assessment together: Lesley asked the questions, Chang'e read the needle. At Selrick, Lesley counts Chang'e's hours of sleep and makes her take her pill. "I hate scary Big Sis!" says Chang'e, and swallows it. On the command deck, at the Singularity, she still calls her Big Sis.

In the Storm Citadel's attack an Ender bent over Chang'e at her console. Chang'e sat still so it would strike and open its chest, and told Lesley to hold her fire for the call. Lesley held, then made the shot. This time Chang'e did not push her away. Lesley said her vow aloud at last: "Ever since that day, I vowed to keep you safe, Chang'e."
change--mr-bunny: Chang'e built Mr. Bunny as a friend when she was small, in the evenings at the end of her parents' bench. He is a white ball with long ears, and his face is a black screen, so he can make faces. He fetched whatever she pointed at while she built Lesley's rifle.

Chang'e calls him her best friend. When Ruby wanted to read his code, Chang'e said she would not let anyone take him away. He floats at her shoulder wherever she goes: in class, in the field, on the command deck. Once, on an avenue, he came at her call as a great white rabbit-head machine taller than the storefronts, and the Enders broke against him.

In the Storm Citadel's attack, Chang'e planned for an Ender to strike at her so its chest would open. "Mr. Bunny takes the hit," she said. He swung in front of her face and took the claw meant for her. He came back dented, one ear crooked, until his screen found its smile and he floated back to her shoulder.
obsidia--selena: Obsidia made Selena. She grew her in the nest, where her kind slept, and changed her face again and again until it was right. On the storm night of 983 she carried the sleeping child down herself and left her in the mud of Terrinia: the first of her making with a perfect human form. Then Obsidia took the Storm Citadel far away, to watch what grew.

Obsidia calls Selena her seed and her pawn. Selena knew her only as the huntress who made her. Selena sold Obsidia last year's Academy numbers for pay, but never a name or a place where people die. Obsidia sent recall after recall, and Selena ignored them all.

When Obsidia's field put out the Aspirants, Selena chose to follow the last recall, and rode her lightning up into the Storm Citadel. "It's been a while, my dear creator," she said. Obsidia tipped up Selena's chin and looked her over like something she had carved herself. Then she bound her in chains of bone. Selena tore them apart and declared war on her maker: "I'll never be your puppet again!"

Selena cut the throne down instead of taking it. Obsidia's weapon went through her side, and a point-blank shot threw her out of the burning ship. As the Citadel was drawn into the Singularity, Obsidia rose in a new form of silver and gold and opened her arms. "Come back, my puppet." Selena thought of Karina and the Academy, and charged. There the story leaves them.
fanny--layla: Fanny came to Selrick two years late, from the Shield. On her first day her time beat Layla's, and Layla, who had never been second, raced her at everything. At a real breach of the dome they argued over who covered whom, then fought back to back on the sand outside it. Layla saw that the Enders were not target practice.

Professor Joe made them the Layla-Fanny Team, with one shared score. Fanny gave Layla a box of chocolate: "This is for you, my teammate!" They held a ward together against a giant, and took the west end of the fish market. When Layla told Guinevere her star was only a circuit, and circuits glitch, Fanny said, "Leave her be, Layla."

Since the sand, Layla had gone first on every raid. When Guinevere flew off alone after Vexana, Layla built a rescue map in the time it took Fanny to give one order. Fanny dropped the Shield's way for it. "Lead," she said.

When the Storm Citadel's field killed every suit, they held a wall across the bay road cut, back to back: Fanny with plain steel, Layla counting each Ender's strike. A crying boy asked Layla if Fanny was her friend. "She's my teammate," said Layla. Fanny said she was not doing it alone.
vexana--vexanas-father: Vexana's father was a soldier of the Shield of Dawnbreak who kept the big guns on the city wall working. They lived in a Shield house under the wall. He taught her to press a bent bracket straight with two fingers. He led her up the wall stair to look out over the dark ground, and gave her a small star of her own.

One evening the guns on the wall all fired at once. Vexana slipped out of the shelter to find him, and an Ender stepped into her path. He stood between her and it and said, "Stay back." It was the last thing he ever said to her. A soldier carried her off. Another told her that Ender never got past him while he stood. The record listed him killed in action, and his toolbox was all that came back.

Vexana blamed herself, and kept everyone away so nobody would die for her again. At the Singularity, facing a tall Ender, she set her boots wide on the stone, the way he had once stood between an Ender and his daughter. Inside the black hole she told Guinevere at last: her father, a soldier, died saving her, and she wished it had been her instead.
change--selena: Chang'e first met Selena at a salvage stall at the city's edge. On it an old servo from her parents' lab turned its arm, mended with a trick Chang'e had never seen. She paid every coin in her pockets and two jelly candies, and told Selena to come to the Science Division's entry. Later Chang'e looked for the girl's face on the entry list and found it, beside the name Selena.
Selena calls her Teacher Chang'e. Chang'e marks Selena's reports, and once called the suit Selena drew in class excellent homework. In the lab they bet puddings on Selena's designs.

On the morning of the Singularity, Chang'e posted Selena as mobile support, because Silverbolt was the fastest machine in her division. When the deck called mobile support to report, the light on the panel only kept blinking.
guinevere--hester: Hester was the first person who ever counted for Guinevere. On the storm night, as the newest guard of House Baroque, she carried the baby down to the cellar, counting the steps so she would not cry. Later she tied the red bows of Guinevere's mother in her hair. Guinevere's father put Hester at the head of his daughter's guard.

Hester had learned to fight from an old Shield sergeant. One dawn she gave in to Guinevere's pestering and taught her: "Elbow in. Hip first. Hands home after every punch." At the Academy, Guinevere still hit the bag bare-fisted the way Hester had taught her. Hester drove her and watched over her, and clapped alone in her row when Guinevere took the top score.

Hester carries the father's orders without softening them. When she brought word to the gate that Guinevere must come home, Guinevere refused, and Hester reminded her: hands home after every punch. Guinevere walked away counting her steps, as Hester once counted the cellar stairs. In the bay road cut, with no drones and no wings, Guinevere heard Hester's voice again and brought her hands home.
karina--selena: Karina is on the rescue team, the people who go into the ruins after a strike. On the storm night of 983 her lamp found a small child in the mud. She knelt and gathered her up, and the child's arms went around her neck and held on. Nobody came to claim the child, so Karina kept her: "You don't put down someone you carried out."

Karina raised her in a two-room flat with the team radio always on, and called it nothing but duty. When the girl named herself, Karina said, "Selena it is." When Selena was late for class, her guardian had already called it in.

On the morning of the attack Karina told her, "Come home after." During the battle she carried a lamp from door to door in the flooded wards. High above the city, when her maker opened her arms to call her back, Selena remembered the lamp in the rain. Somebody down there still wanted to see her graduate. Selena charged.
vexana--will-of-the-planet: In Chang'e's class the Will of the Planet was only a word on a screen: the mind behind the Enders. When an Ender dragged Vexana into the void, she says, the Will came to her as a giant in dark violet armor and showed her the end, with Guinevere lying broken. It marked her with a cold point in her chest.

Vexana decided to let it use her. She would take its orders, walk among its Enders as one of them, and keep close to its body. The orders came through the mark: a place and a time, never a reason. She obeyed them as cover.

In the Storm Citadel, Obsidia told Vexana the Will did not hate humans. Then it could not be begged, Vexana decided. It had to be broken. She went on obeying. On the morning of the attack the order came as a voice inside her: "The Academy. Now." Its Enders ran with her as if she led them.
lesley--lesleys-brother: Lesley's little brother followed her from room to room and held on to her leg. She was Sis to him, and he never called her anything else. Every night he held her sleeve and asked what would happen if an Ender came. "Then I'll stand in front," she told him, every night.

In 983 an Ender broke the house. Lesley stepped in front of him, and it took her left eye. "Sis?" he said behind her: his last word. In the morning she found his hand under a beam, and it did not hold on. She had kept her promise, and he died anyway. After that she promised nobody anything.

Years later, at the research base, Chang'e held her sleeve the same way and asked her to promise, and Lesley did. In the Storm Citadel's attack, when an Ender bent over Chang'e, Lesley's feet started round the chair to stand in front, as she had told her brother every night. Chang'e told her to stay at her back.
change--guinevere: Chang'e taught Guinevere's class. She told them the Will of the Planet sends the Enders, and that the readings suggest it has a body, the Mother Matrix. Under a tree Guinevere repeated the lesson to Vexana: to defeat the Will, they must destroy the Enders' Control Core hidden in its dark void.

When Vexana went missing, Chang'e reminded Guinevere what she had told her class: she would never send a student anywhere she could not bring them back from. Nobody had sent Vexana. Chang'e could not even find the door, so she sent Guinevere to Ruby. At the Singularity, Guinevere saw with her own eyes the Mother Matrix she had heard of in Teacher Chang'e's class.
change--vexana: Chang'e taught Vexana's class. She named the void, the dark behind the world where the Enders come from, and said nobody could get near it. She also taught them a rule about a planet that holds Balance and a people grown too strong.

Then an Ender dragged Vexana into that dark. In the Storm Citadel she put Chang'e's rule to Obsidia: who gave a planet the right? In the hollow she told Obsidia, "Our teacher said nobody can get near this dark." "Your teacher was right," said Obsidia. The Will opens every door into it, and Obsidia opens her own.
guinevere--guineveres-father: Guinevere's father holds the head seat on the board of House Baroque. He lost his wife to the Enders, and Guinevere came to think he answered everything with money: he lost her mother and bought walls. When she brought him her first page of sums, held up to the gap in his office door, it came back with a red mark.

At Selrick she wrote to him every week, with every sum her tutors set, and began every letter with the word Father. He never answered. His seat stayed empty at her trial. When she took the top score, all she got was a cold rebuke: "Stop being so stubborn and focus more on the family business!"

After Vexana was taken, he sent word through Hester: come home, or lose her place in the House. Guinevere did not go. Inside the black hole she told Vexana all of it, and said she would give up being a lady of status and start over rather than back down.
layla--professor-joe: Professor Joe teaches the Combat Division, and Layla was on his Team B3. In his class she said an Ender's weak spot shows when it attacks, as if it were easy. On the day of the breach, Joe knelt on the avenue over a crying girl with a pink rabbit and covered her from a falling slab. Layla walked away to argue over who covered whom.

Joe came back on a cane. He dissolved Team B3 and made Layla and Fanny the Layla-Fanny Team, with one shared score: a kill is a point, a civilian carried clear is ten. At the gate portal he sends their team to its place on each raid.

In the bay road cut, Fanny knelt by a crying boy and spoke to him softly. Layla had heard that voice once before, from Joe on the avenue the day of the breach. That day she had caught the voice but not the words. Maybe they were the same words.
angela--guinevere: When Vexana went missing, Angela held Guinevere's star in her cupped hands. It could not point, only say yes. "Then yes is something," said Angela. Each night Guinevere searched the sky from the observation lab Angela and Ruby kept. On the third night Angela pushed a stool over to the telescope for her. At lunch, when Layla doubted the star, Angela said, "I came back once. People come back."

At the Singularity, Guinevere came low across the water with Enders swarming her, and Angela opened a pane in her shield and pulled her through. Guinevere's star was blazing. Angela opened a pane wide enough for one and sent her on: "Go, Guinevere, pursue your light."
change--changes-father: Chang'e's father was one of the two chief scientists of Terrinia's research base. He and Chang'e's mother brought her there before she could walk properly and raised her as their daughter. She called him Dad. He was a quiet man who counted by ear, and his hands set the smallest parts of Lesley's eye.

On the night the base fell, his voice stayed calm. "Stay close, Chang'e," he said, and counted the steps to the shelter. Then a black-and-gold giant turned its light on the yard. He and Chang'e's mother shoved her clear and stood in front of her. When she could see again, the crater where they stood was empty.
change--changes-mother: Chang'e's mother was the other chief scientist of the research base, a warm, laughing woman. With Chang'e's father she raised Chang'e as their daughter, and Chang'e called her Mom. She began every project by writing who it was for. She set a fourth plate at supper for Lesley, and promised at the gate to keep setting it.

On the night the base fell, she did up the top button of Chang'e's coat and held her hand across the yard, calling Lesley on the radio. Lesley did not answer. When the black-and-gold giant opened its chest, she let go of Chang'e's hand. She and Chang'e's father shoved Chang'e clear and stood in its light. The crater where they stood was empty.
fanny--lesley: Lesley, the Chief Combat Instructor, signed Fanny in on her first day at Selrick. "Fanny. Transfer. Two years with the Shield. You asked for the front." Then her one visible eye went to Fanny's hands. "One without the Aspirant spirit is like a gun without bullets."

On the day Ruby and Angela became Aspirants, Lesley stood before Fanny, Layla, Ruby and Angela in the Academy hall. "We still don't fully understand our own power. But by trusting each other, we can gain limitless strength." In the Storm Citadel's attack she gave the frontline its ground on the channel, and Fanny answered, "Understood."
guinevere--guineveres-mother: Guinevere's mother looks down from a portrait at the far end of the long hall of the House, with a lamp burning under it. On the storm night she was working late at the House's bank by the harbor, and she did not come home. Hester told it to Guinevere once, when she was small enough to ask.

When the House cleared her rooms, Hester kept back two red bows from her dressing table and tied them in Guinevere's hair. After that Guinevere tied them herself and let no one else touch them, until Vexana reached over on the day of the badges and set one straight. After Vexana was taken, the left bow kept coming out crooked.
guinevere--layla: On Team-Up Day, the day cadets chose partners, Guinevere and Layla both stood alone. Their eyes met across the courtyard, and neither would walk over to the other. For two years after, they shared classes, and neither ever spoke first. Before the fish-market raid Guinevere spoke first: "You're Layla. I'm the great lady Guinevere. Nobody's introduced us."

After Vexana was taken, Layla told Guinevere that portals don't give people back. When Guinevere flew off alone after Vexana, Layla had a rescue map ready, and Lesley sent her team to Guinevere. Layla had called Vexana a traitor. Now, under the Mother Matrix, she counted angles for her.

Layla's plan drew the Matrix's fire down at Angela's shield, away from Guinevere and Vexana, so its chest would open. "Guinevere," she said on the channel. "When it looks at us, it's yours." The chest opened, and Guinevere and Vexana struck it together.
guinevere--professor-joe: Guinevere was the pink-haired girl from Professor Joe's class. At the breach of the dome she fought up close with her fists and drones, with Vexana above her. On the day of the fish-market raid, Joe, still on his cane, sent Guinevere and Vexana to the east end.

In the bay road cut, with no drones and no wings, Guinevere hit an Ender's chest a moment too late: the plates had shut while she ducked. She remembered Joe's lesson. They don't strike easily, and when one does, that is how long you get.
layla--lesley: Lesley is the Chief Combat Instructor of Selrick. On the day Ruby and Angela became Aspirants, she stood before Layla, Fanny, Ruby and Angela in the Academy hall and told them that by trusting each other they could gain limitless strength.

At the Singularity Lesley commanded from the deck, and Layla took her orders on the channel. When something took the Mother Matrix's shot for Guinevere, Lesley told Layla where Guinevere was and to get to her if she could. "Copy," said Layla, over the roar of her cannon.
